title: Regression incident synthesis and action log
body:
Purpose:
This working note captures synthesis from the 2026-03-08 performance alerts across eu-west-1 and us-west-2, the bisect/benchmark runs we executed, and the concrete remediation steps and follow-ups. Designed to be the single source for the incident timeline, quick hypotheses, profiling artifacts, and an ownerable action list that can be handed to SRE/serving-runtime/product.

Executive summary:
- Between 2026-03-07 22:30 UTC and 2026-03-08 02:10 UTC we saw a 15–25% P95 latency uplift for the hosted text-generation endpoint backed by gpt-lite-3-8b-quant across two regions. Error rate (5xx) remained low but timeouts increased for tail requests.
- Initial dashboard signals pointed to increased per-request tokenization cost and a small but sustained increase in KV cache misses for long-running sessions.
- Canary diff (canary build: runtime v3.14.1 vs baseline v3.13.8) showed regressions only on models with per-request sequence > 512; small models (<128) unaffected.

Data sources and dashboards inspected:
- perf/serving/p95-by-model (Grafana): time-range 2026-03-07 20:00 -> 2026-03-08 04:00, grouped by model, region, instance-type. Query snapshot id: graf-ps-20260308-01.
- cache/kv/miss-rate (Influx): showed a jump from 2.1% -> 7.4% on session-keyspace for long context sessions.
- prod-traces/streaming (Jaeger): sampled 120 traces, focused on tokenization -> prefill -> generation stages.
- canary-diffs/last-run (S3): s3://redwood-canary-diffs/2026-03-08/v3.14.1-v3.13.8/report.html
- local-benchmarks/ci (artifacts): ci/bench/gpt-lite-3-8b/2026-03-08/{latency,profile}.json

Timeline (high level):
- 2026-03-07 22:28 UTC: perf-sentinel alert (P95 > 1400ms) triggered for eu-west-1.
- 22:35: oncall paged, Slack created (#perf-incident-4285).
- 22:42: quick triage: CPU and GPU saturation metrics normal; per-host token throughput unchanged.
- 23:05: canary comparison job kicked off between v3.14.1 and v3.13.8 with identical traffic replay.
- 23:40: profiling samples indicate tokenization stage increased 2–3x CPU user time for requests > 1024 tokens.
- 00:15: bisect plan executed: rolled back a subset of runtime changes (kernel selection heuristics) in a shadow cluster.
- 01:35: partial rollback reduced P95 by ~10% but not back to baseline; KV cache miss remained elevated.
- 02:00: concluded likely multi-factor regression: tokenization CPU path + cache churn due to cache-key encoding change (recent commit).

Hypotheses and evidence: (ranked)
1) Tokenization micro-optimizer introduced a regression for long sequences (HIGH).
   - Evidence: profiler flamegraphs (ci/profile/tokenizer-20260308.svg) show increased user CPU in unicode normalization path after patch.
   - Repro: run local bench with long-context corpus (bench/long-context-9k) reproduces 18% higher tokenization time.
2) KV cache key encoding tweak changed eviction pattern (MED).
   - Evidence: cache miss rate jump concurrent with config deploy. Cache logs show shorter TTLs for a subset of keys.
   - Repro: synthetic workload with same session-id distribution reproduces miss increase.
3) Subtle GC pressure from a dependency bump in the streaming layer leading to tail latency (LOW).
   - Evidence: GC pause metrics small but slightly elevated on a subset of pods. No direct correlating spikes with P95.

Bisect and canary comparison notes:
- Approach: keep traffic replay identical between canary and baseline; capture CPU/gpu counters, per-stage timings, and kv-metrics. Use diff-runner to compute per-request latencies and stage deltas.
- Key result: stage-delta graph (s3 artifact) shows tokenization stage accounts for +120ms median for long requests on v3.14.1. Generation stage unchanged.
- Canary lesson: splitting canaries by sequence-length bucket is essential; aggregating across all traffic masks regressions that only affect long contexts.

Profiling artifacts collected (links / artifact ids):
- profiler: ci/profile/tokenizer-20260308.pb.gz
- flamegraph: ci/profile/tokenizer-20260308.svg
- heap-snapshot: ci/profile/heap-20260308.heapsnap
- per-request trace ids: trace-20260308-{0001..0120} (saved to s3)

Immediate mitigations attempted and results:
- Reverted tokenizer micro-optimizer patch in a shadow canary -> P95 reduced by ~8% on long requests but KV miss unchanged.
- Increased KV cache size on a small ring (10% capacity bump) -> small reduction in misses but still above baseline.
- Applied temporary routing rule to prefer instances with warm cache (manual sticky-routing) -> tail latency improved for top 10% sessions.

Action items (owners and rough ETA):
- A1: Full revert of tokenizer micro-optimizer and write a minimized benchmark reproducer (owner: Daniel Park, due: 2026-03-12)
- A2: Cache-key encoding audit and repro harness; add integration test to simulate session churn (owner: Sofia Martinez, due: 2026-03-18)
- A3: Expand canary matrix to include sequence-length buckets and cache-warmth dimension (owner: Ravi Krishnan, due: 2026-03-15)
- A4: Add alert that splits P95 by sequence-length percentiles (owner: Anika Rao, due: 2026-03-13)
- A5: Post-mortem doc with timeline + learnings (owner: Anika Rao, due: 2026-03-20)

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Is the cache-key TTL change intended in the recent config push? Who approved it? (TODO: link change-id)
- Are there any other model families showing the same symptom but masked because of different request-length distribution?
- Should we add a canary test that specifically exercises long streaming sessions end-to-end (including prefix caching)?

Notes to reviewer:
- This file is intentionally concise and operational: the raw artifacts live in the linked_artifacts and S3 buckets. Please add comments inline for any missing repro cases or if you want additional sampling windows.
- If you are taking ownership of an action item, reply in the incident Slack thread and update the Linear ticket.

Appendix: quick commands used during triage (copy/paste friendly)
- curl "https://grafana/api/datasources/proxy/1/api/v1/query_range?query=p95_latency_by_model&start=..." > ./tmp/p95.json
- redis-cli --csv HGETALL kv:session:metrics | grep miss_rate
- pytest tests/bench/test_long_context.py -k tokenizer --bench

End of log.
